entry.title: Unreasoned Within Reason
entry.summary: I want to teach you a new term. Orthogonal bets. Oar.
entry.content:
I want to teach you a new term.

Orthogonal bets.

Oar.

Thog.

Gonal.

Now, it may not be new to you, but if it is, it is.

Orthogonal is a fancy way to say 90 degrees.

Perpendicular.

Which is also fancy.

X goes up.

Y goes right.

Never the two shall cross.

I suppose they do at you, though.

You are the cross(roads).

I read it in two ways.

Maybe more.

One is if everybody zigging.

You zag.

Everyone zagging.

You zig.

You dig?

And if all you do is zag.

Maybe somethings you zig.

Or if zig, then zag.

You can call it a hedge, I suppose.

Hedge on your life.

If you're into that.

But I really think this is where all the asymmetric stuff is.

The fun stuff.

If everyone is going one way.

Or if you are.

Maybe you go the other way.

You turn right.

Or left.

Not all the time, now.

All the time gets you in trouble.

Just enough.

To keep things interesting.

Keep things fresh.

If all you do is digital.

Be a little analog.

And versa vice.

All you do is highways.

Take the local route.

Like Bob Frost said.

Take the road less traveled.

Makes all the difference.

Start making orthogonal bets.

Don't make it the main thing.

Unless you want to.

Just enough to be unreasonable.

Within reason.

"Are you going to help me or not?"

"Alright, alright, alright!

I'll tell you what to do:

Go that way.

Really fast.

If something gets in your way,

Turn."

⛷

👈

[Watching you ragdoll down a mountain].

Alright!

Now, turn!!!

🎩

entry.title: September And Everything After
entry.summary: Time's so interesting. How interesting is it? I'll look back at…
entry.content:
Time's so interesting.

How interesting is it?

I'll look back at something I thought I've had for years and we bought it in March.

Our "newest" ride has now been with us for almost a decade.

Feels like five years.

Six max.

You might say that's close enough.

But it's not.

It flew.

And sometimes it doesn't.

It lounges.

I like to say "I can't remember my life before..."

And I mean this life.

Now, of course I can.

I can remember it.

But I cannot feel it.

Not the same way.

Not like I used to.

I know I did it.

I know I lived it.

But it just feels like a memory.

Like a first person perspective movie.

Just something I watched happen.

Or played through.

Where am I going with this?

Who knows.

Who ever knows.

Sometimes, I rhyme slow.

Sometimes, I rhyme quick.

🎤

Time rhymes.

Some of the time.

And I know poetry doesn't have to.

But I sure do love it when it does.

You didn't rhyme.

Do.

Ok, it's time.

To decades in seconds.

And the longest hours.

And everything after.

entry.title: Sugar Pie Honey Bunches of Hall and Oat(e)s
entry.summary: We live in a world, now more than ever, where if…
entry.content:
We live in a world, now more than ever, where if it sounds too good to be true.

It probably is.

Too good to be true.

Which is a weird, almost positive, way to say it's not true.

And sure, we all encounter that on a daily basis.

Hourly basis.

Minutely basis.

We're unable now to trust our eyes and ears.

If we ever were.

I think it started with those filters that dewrinkled you.

Smoothed it out.

Made you purty(ish).

Now it don't even have to be you.

You just tell it to be.

And it is.

Magic.

I think you can still trust smells.

Touches.

Tastes.

For now.

But see and hear?

Untrustable.

Now, you should always trust your sixth sense.

If you got one.

I used to think everyone did.

But they don't.

Your spidey sense.

If that sheet tingles, you always trust it.

That sheet tapping quantum.

But to me, that means we got three senses left.

Four tops.

Great band.

Or maybe it means we gotta develop new senses.

Hunches.

Trust those.

Inner voices.

Like me.

Trust those (kinda).

Hey!

And your heart.

Aww.

These things.

These senses.

Will let you down.

Sure, like all things.

But it's also important to know that it will let you up.

And that's where I'm going.

So come on up, too.

Always room up here.

Actually.

Ackchyually.

I can't go for that.

No can do.

Pick another mountain.

This one is out of touch.

Haha, can't help myself.

🔊

Soul really matters to me.

Too much.

entry.title: Like A Sumo
entry.summary: I'm getting kinda fat. There I said it. Dad bod. My…
entry.content:
I'm getting kinda fat.

There I said it.

Dad bod.

My older (younger) body liked nay loved the iron.

This newer (oldish) body don't.

It just don't.

It likes aluminum.

Lined bags.

Filled with Doritos.

Awful.

Yummy.

Just awful.

The older, younger, body let me down.

Sure, it was fast(ish).

Strong(ish).

But it broke down.

Left me by the side of the road.

Almost totaled.

Almost.

Sure, it could lift more than 225 over my head for reps (seated military) but that strength means nothing if you deed.

If you deed.

Now I lift aluminum cans.

Much lighter weights.

More reps.

Counter to lips.

Over and over.

Not the healthiest way to do things.

It's just coke zero. No beers.

But I'm here to do things.

Not deed.

And the best part of having this new, old(ish), fattish body is that it comes with this brain, man.

This brain thinks differently.

These eyes see with different lenses.

And this heart feels fuller, somehow.

Maybe that's where all the muscle went.

So thankful.

So grateful.

So blessed.

To be getting fat.

Insane.

"Fat boy on a diet.

Don't try it."

entry.title: Booth Or Tablet
entry.summary: If I was in the mood to mentor, I'd pick a…
entry.content:
If I was in the mood to mentor, I'd pick a booth.

Huh?

Like say you called me up.

How the heck they get this number?

I don't answer.

I don't see it.

You leave voicemail.

I get to it eventually.

We set up a lunch.

I pick a booth.

That's where I like to mentor.

A booth.

Tables aren't it.

I'm a booth guy.

Can't mentor at a table.

Or a tablet.

📱

Maybe you can.

Of course, I don't mentor.

I'm retired.

Ohhh, that's why.

I don't like that word.

So let's call me secluded.

I'm secluded.

Where was I?

Oh, yes, mentorsheet.

When I did, I notice looking back that they were all in booths.

Mostly in booths.

Might have been a table once or twice.

I'm not a guy who stands up and talks to a crowd and owns the room.

I don't do that.

I'm a guy who booths.

I can own a booth.

Or used to.

A guy who owned booths.

Booth owner.

I think they call it introverted.

But I'm just outroverted.

🍽

So, why am I sitting here?

Did you order apps?

Where's my two coke zeros?

You put anything in this?

Smells funny.

Get a pitcher of zero.

Work on that.

I gotta use the can.

This man walking around here like he's Ray Kroc.

entry.title: Kinda Mean
entry.summary: Part of the deal that comes with being an old(ish) curmudgeon…
entry.content:
Part of the deal that comes with being an old(ish) curmudgeon is you gotta be mad.

It's kinda crucial to the whole gimmick.

Outraged.

Cantankerous.

Great word.

So what do you make of an old(ish) curmudgeon who's just having the time of his life?

Grinning through the madness.

The only way to go.

There's an old line that I like to quote.

About how New Yorkers are not nice but they are kind.

And how Californians are nice but they are not kind.

And the example I heard recently was if you had something in your teeth.

That a New Yorker would say, "Hey fool, you got something in your teeth."

Not nice, but kind.

Whereas the Californian would just let you walk around with it.

And how the line in that song that's really just a commencement speech talks about living in New York City once but to leave before it makes you hard.

And the same for Northern California but leaving before it makes you soft.

But the teeth thing isn't really right.

It's more like this.

The kind not nice thing.

Let's move away from oral hygiene.

There's an old movie with Will Smith.

Back when it was ok to like him.

He was chasing something, then.

He's homeless and trying to make a living with a young son.

The details aren't important.

But he's in the city.

And he's running to cross the street at lunch hour.

A car hits him.

Boom!

And the guy gets out and looks genuinely concerned for Will.

"Hey arsehole. Are you okay, arsehole?"

That's not nice but kind.

Although it's a movie.

Set in San Francisco.

So maybe it's a city thing.

Not a state.

But that's the difference.

The other way would be to be really nice to Will, getting his contact information so you could later sue him (hopefully well insured and/or net worth it) for the damage to your car, emotional distress, hospital bills, physical therapy, loss of consortium, etc.

Or to avoid same.

Nice, not kind.

See the difference?

It's like that line Southerners say.

"Bless your heart."

Can be a polite insult.

The city way to say that is "What the fook wrong with you?"

So I leave you with this:

Nice and kind are not the same.

Not even similar.

And the nicest people you will encounter may be the worst.

And the kindest may seem a little rough around the center.

This is exceptional, of course.

Most nice people are decent.

Likable.

Most kind people are obviously so.

Radiant.

And the other way, too.

But sometimes, just sometimes, the maddest dog in the kennel, is also the sweetest.

🐺

Oh, I wasn't referring to me.

I'm a dragon.

🐲

Are you okay?

I'm fine, fool.

Say, what's your name?

Are you judgment proof?

Next!!!

entry.title: Actualization
entry.summary: I don't want you to get the wrong idea. I want…
entry.content:
I don't want you to get the wrong idea.

I want you to get the right idea.

So which ones do you get?

I'm hoping the latter.

But as we all know, ideas are everywhere.

Free and contagious.

Wrong idea gets you, whooo boy.

It keels ya.

But a right one.

A right one.

Goes the other way.

It births ya.

Now a good idea only gets you so far.

You need to act upon the idea.

To turn it from thought into thing.

Iterating on the thing over and over until it gets closer to perfection, or at least, its peak.

Good enough.

I would call it Actualization, but hey, I already did.

It's kinda the point.

The whole point.

To all of this.

[Hands waving in random, dramatic, circles.]

Meh.

Just an idea.

What do I know?

💭 to ♾ to ⏏️

entry.title: Asian Raisins
entry.summary: I don't feel old. I mean, I sorta do. Oldish. Energy…
entry.content:
I don't feel old.

I mean, I sorta do.

Oldish.

Energy on low.

Vibes on high.

Me in the middle.

Just happy to be here.

But I look in the mirror and I can still see youngish me.

Signs of him.

Particularly since I shaved the locks off.

The lion's mane, mane.

I was looking like Steven Seagal.

Which, all due respect to the Glimmer Man, I wasn't really going for.

Asian don't raisin.

Did I make that up?

I don't want to search if I did.

So let's just say I did.

Taking credit, whether or not it's due.

Unless you really old, then you sorta look like a raisin.

If you're Asian.

And lucky enough to ferment.

Some lady turned 117 recently.

Not Asian, but still quite raisiny.

To dried grapes.

Aging like fine wine.

🍇
